question: Which amendment act added the Fundamental duties in the constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: 44th Constitutional Amendment Act
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act
51st Constitutional Amendment Act
38th Constitutional Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976). This amendment was based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. The Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A. Initially, there were 10 duties; later, the 86th Amendment (2002) added one more duty (providing opportunities for education to children aged 6-14 years), making a total of 11 Fundamental Duties. These duties remind citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation and create a balance with fundamental rights.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Amendment that added Fundamental Duties → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ Article describing Fundamental Duties → Article 51A
☛ Total number of Fundamental Duties → 11
☛ Duty added by 86th Amendment → Providing education opportunities to children aged 6-14
☛ Committee that recommended Fundamental Duties → Swaran Singh Committee

question: Which of the following has the right to make parliamentary law in relation to Scheduled Areas? (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Ministers of Cabinet
Governor
Parliament
State Legislature
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor

Explanation:
Under Article 244 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor has the right to make parliamentary laws related to Scheduled Areas. The Governor can issue special regulations for the welfare of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. Parts IX and IX-A of the Constitution empower the Governor to regulate the functioning of Panchayats and Municipalities in these areas. The Governor can also decide which laws of the state legislature apply to Scheduled Areas, with modifications if needed. This power ensures the protection and development of tribal communities. The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas, while the Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas in northeastern states. The Governor's role is crucial in safeguarding the rights and interests of these vulnerable groups.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Authority to make laws for Scheduled Areas → Governor
☛ Article 244 deals with → Scheduled and Tribal Areas
☛ Who controls Panchayats in Scheduled Areas → Governor
☛ Fifth Schedule contains → Administration of Scheduled Areas
☛ Sixth Schedule contains → Administration of Tribal Areas
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसे अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों के संबंध में संसदीय कानून बनाने का अधिकार है? (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)

संसद
राज्य विधायिका

Explanation:
अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों से संबंधित संसदीय कानून बनाने का अधिकार भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 244 के तहत राज्यपाल को दिया गया है। अनुसूचित क्षेत्र और अनुसूचित जनजाति के कल्याण के लिए राज्यपाल विशेष नियम बना सकते हैं। संविधान के भाग IX और IX-A के तहत, राज्यपाल को अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों में पंचायतों और नगरपालिकाओं के कामकाज को विनियमित करने का अधिकार है। राज्यपाल यह भी निर्धारित कर सकते हैं कि कौन से कानून अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों पर लागू होंगे। राज्यपाल के पास वहाँ के शासन में सुधार के लिए आदेश जारी करने की शक्ति है। यह प्रावधान अनुसूचित जनजातियों के हितों की रक्षा करता है और उनके विकास को सुनिश्चित करता है।

question: The powers, rights and duties of Panchayats were included in the 11th Schedule of the Constitution by ______. (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: 69th Amendment Act
92nd Amendment Act
74th Amendment Act
73rd Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 73rd Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 73rd Amendment Act of 1992 granted constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions in India. It added Part IX and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution. The 11th Schedule lists 29 subjects related to the powers, rights, and duties of Panchayats. This amendment aimed to strengthen rural local self-government and promote decentralization. The 74th Amendment deals with urban local bodies (municipalities).

question: The oath or administration of state ministers comes under which schedule of the Constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Fifth Schedule
Second Schedule
Fourth Schedule
Third Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Third Schedule

Explanation:
The Third Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the forms of oaths or affirmations for various office holders, such as the President, Vice President, members of the Council of Ministers, State Ministers, judges, etc. The oath format for state ministers is also included in this schedule. According to Article 164, before entering office, a state minister takes an oath in the form prescribed in the Third Schedule. This oath is administered by the Governor of the state. Therefore, the oath-taking of state ministers comes under the Third Schedule.

भारतीय संविधान की तीसरी अनुसूची में विभिन्न पदाधिकारियों, जैसे राष्ट्रपति, उपराष्ट्रपति, मंत्रिपरिषद के सदस्य, राज्य मंत्रियों, न्यायाधीशों आदि के लिए शपथ या प्रतिज्ञान के प्रारूप दिए गए हैं। राज्य मंत्रियों की शपथ का प्रारूप भी इसी अनुसूची में शामिल है। अनुच्छेद 164 के अनुसार, राज्य के मंत्री पद ग्रहण करने से पहले तीसरी अनुसूची में दिए गए प्रारूप के अनुसार शपथ लेते हैं। यह शपथ राज्य के राज्यपाल द्वारा दिलाई जाती है। इस प्रकार, राज्य मंत्रियों का शपथ-ग्रहण तीसरी अनुसूची के अंतर्गत आता है।

question: Who was the chairperson of the commission which was set up to determine the relationship between the Center and the states? (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: M.M. Punchhi
S .K Dhar
P. V. Rajamannar
R. S. Sarkaria
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is M.M. Punchhi

Explanation:
In 2007, the central government set up a commission under the chairmanship of M.M. Punchhi to review the relationship between the Centre and states. The commission was formally called the Commission on Centre-State Relations. It submitted its report in 2010, offering suggestions on the division of powers, the role of the governor, and the use of Article 356. Earlier, the R.S. Sarkaria Commission (1983-88) had also reported on the same subject. The Punchhi Commission recommended clear guidelines for the appointment and tenure of governors, among other things. Its recommendations remain important for understanding federal dynamics in India.

question: Who has the right to provide permanent residency to the local residents of Jammu and Kashmir? (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)

President
Parliament

solution:

question: Amendment in the Directive Principle of State Policy is done on the basis of _________. (RPF SI 2018 (06/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Simple majority
Special majority of parliament with consent of states
Special majority of both the houses of Parliament
Full majority
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Special majority of both the houses of Parliament

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution. Under Article 368, amendments to DPSP require a special majority of both houses of Parliament, meaning a two-thirds majority of members present and voting. This amendment procedure differs from Fundamental Rights, which may require consent of states. DPSP aim to establish social and economic justice and are non-justiciable, but they play a crucial role in policy-making. The special majority ensures stability in these principles. Unlike some constitutional amendments, no state ratification is needed for DPSP amendments.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which majority is required to amend DPSP? → Special majority of both houses of Parliament
☛ Which Article deals with amendment procedure? → Article 368
☛ In which part of Constitution are DPSP found? → Part IV

question: If the President returns the bill for reconsideration of the Parliament then it is called _____  (RPF SI 2018 (10/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Suspension Veto (Veto)
Limited veto (veto)
Pocket Veto (Veto)
Complete veto (veto)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Suspension Veto

Explanation:
When the President returns a bill to the Parliament for reconsideration, it is called a Suspension Veto. This is a type of veto power where the President suspends the bill by sending it back with suggestions. If the Parliament passes the bill again, the President is bound to give his assent. The Suspension Veto applies only to ordinary bills, not to money bills. It limits the President's power because once the Parliament re-passes the bill, the President must accept it. This veto is a unique feature of the Indian Constitution, balancing the powers between the executive and the legislature.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ On which bills does Suspension Veto not apply? → Money Bills
☛ What action is required from the President after Parliament re-passes a bill? → Must give assent
☛ How many types of veto does the Indian President have? → Three – Suspension, Pocket, Absolute
☛ What happens in a Pocket Veto? → President takes no action on the bill
☛ When is Absolute Veto used? → When the President rejects the bill entirely

question: Business, commerce and movement within India are described in which part of the Constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (10/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Part-IV
Part-XIV
Part-XI
Part-XIII
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part-XIII

Explanation:
Part-XIII of the Indian Constitution deals with 'Trade, Commerce and Intercourse within the territory of India'. It comprises Articles 301 to 307. Article 301 declares that trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India shall be free. However, states have the power to impose reasonable restrictions in public interest. This part ensures the free flow of goods and services across the country, promoting economic unity and national integration. Its objective is to prevent barriers to inter-state trade and maintain a single economic market. Part-IV relates to Directive Principles, Part-XI to Centre-State relations, and Part-XIV to Services under the Union and States.

☛ Article 304 → Allows states to impose reasonable restrictions on trade in public interest.
☛ Article 307 → Empowers Parliament to appoint authority for carrying out purposes of Articles 301-306.

question: From which Constitution, the ideas of freedom, equality and brotherhood given in the preamble of our Constitution have been taken?  (RPF SI 2018 (10/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Australian
Germany's Weimar Constitution
USA
French
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is French

Explanation:
The ideas of 'liberty, equality and fraternity' in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution have been taken from the French Constitution. These three principles are derived from the ideals of the French Revolution (1789), which inspired democratic values worldwide. The framers of the Indian Constitution adopted these principles to establish a just and egalitarian society. The term 'fraternity' was added to emphasize national unity and integrity. It is noteworthy that the Concurrent List was taken from Australia, Emergency provisions from the Weimar Constitution (Germany), and Fundamental Rights from the USA.

question: Under which article of the Indian Constitution, can the President issue the Ordinance?  (RPF SI 2018 (10/01/2019) Shift 1)

Article 143
Article 123
Article 76
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 123

Explanation:

This provision allows the executive to address urgent legislative needs without waiting for Parliament to convene.

question: What is the principle policy of the state taken from the Constitution?  (RPF SI 2018 (10/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Canadian Constitution
Australian Constitution
Irish Constitution
Russian (Russian) Constitution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Irish Constitution

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution are taken from the Irish Constitution. The Irish Constitution incorporated the concept of social justice and a welfare state, which was adopted by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in the Indian Constitution. These principles guide the government in making policies, though they are not enforceable by courts. Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution contains 15 DPSP, based on Gandhian, Socialist, and Liberal-Intellectual principles. Other elements borrowed from the Irish Constitution include the method of election of the President and the nomination system. The DPSP aim to establish social and economic democracy.

question: Who among the following can preside over a joint sitting of the two Houses of the Indian Parliament?  (RPF SI 2018 (10/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Chief Minister of any one of the states
Prime Minister of India
Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Speaker of the Lok Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 108 of the Indian Constitution, the joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides. The joint sitting is summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock over a bill that is passed by one House but rejected or amended by the other. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice President of India) cannot preside, as they are not a member of Rajya Sabha. Neither the Prime Minister nor a Chief Minister is authorized for this role. So far, three joint sittings have occurred: 1961 (Dowry Prohibition Bill), 1978 (MPs and Judicial Immunity), and 2002 (POTA).

अनुच्छेद 370 भारतीय संविधान का वह अनुच्छेद था जो जम्मू और कश्मीर राज्य को विशेष दर्जा प्रदान करता था। यह अनुच्छेद 17 अक्टूबर 1949 को संविधान में जोड़ा गया था और 5 अगस्त 2019 को निरस्त कर दिया गया। इसके तहत जम्मू और कश्मीर को अपना संविधान बनाने, ध्वज रखने और केंद्र सरकार के कई कानूनों से छूट प्राप्त थी। रक्षा, विदेश मामले और संचार जैसे विषयों पर ही केंद्र का अधिकार था। अन्य राज्यों जैसे हरियाणा, मिजोरम और अरुणाचल प्रदेश पर अनुच्छेद 370 लागू नहीं होता था।
